payload.name: Zeigarnik effect
payload.fact: The unfinishedness of events is spontaneously extracted and prioritized in visual processing, leading to more precise memory for unfinished visual paths compared to completed ones.
payload.boundary: The effect is observed in memory recall tasks.

provenance.title: A Zeigarnik-like Effect in the Recall of Anagram Solutions
provenance.quote_or_locus: subjects remembered items they had failed to complete almost twice as often as those they had solved

provenance.title: Interruption, recall and resumption: a meta-analysis of the Zeigarnik and Ovsiankina effects
provenance.quote_or_locus: The memory advantage of unfinished tasks ( Zeigarnik effect) is widely known

provenance.title: The “unfinishedness” of dynamic events is spontaneously extracted in visual processing: A new ‘Visual Zeigarnik Effect’
provenance.quote_or_locus: Although this manipulation was entirely task-irrelevant, it nevertheless had a powerful influence on visual memory: observers placed probes much closer to their correct locations on Unfinished trials
